title: ASCII relief
description: A folded ring is rebuilt from a few precisely drawn glyphs instead of pixels.
useCase: Turn tonal imagery into a scalable typographic treatment with controllable glyph density.
reducedMotion: The elapsed-time clock stops. Parameter controls immediately update the static composition.
limitations: Requires WebGL 1; a static CSS swatch appears if unavailable or after context loss. A procedural four-glyph set rendered in GLSL; no font dependency, imported image, or DOM text conversion.
look: Burgundy ASCII glyphs (dots, plus signs, hash bars and boxes) forming a shaded oval ring on warm off-white paper, set in a fixed character grid.
motion: The ring slowly rocks back and forth (about ±9° on a 31 s sine) and its shading re-quantises into glyphs every frame; a character-size slider changes cell size.
adapt: In `FRAGMENT`, `scene` returns the lit ring's brightness and `glyph` maps it to four 5×7 glyphs by threshold; cell size is `mix(5.,15.,u_control)`. Replace `scene` with your own luminance source, retune the `value` thresholds, and recolour `paper` and `ink`.
